findings.title: Post-preflight read failures are misreported as docType failures
findings.description: `validateFile()` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)` at `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:95`, but that helper silently catches all read failures and returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:63-65`). If a file becomes unreadable after preflight (`packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:73-87`), line 96 treats it as a missing `docType` and returns a normal failed result; the explicit `readFile` catch at lines 101-105 is never reached. The CLI then prints results and sets exit code 1 (`packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:72-85`) instead of routing a typed usage/template error through `handleError(err, 2)` at lines 100-105. This also conflicts with the project rule against silent fallback values. Read the document once with explicit error handling and use that text for both frontmatter parsing and heading checks; add a post-preflight read-failure test. `packages/core/tests/schema/sliceDesignFiles.test.ts:117-124` only covers preflight `access()` failures.

findings.title: Guide template is read without initializing the guide checkout
findings.description: `resolveTemplatePath()` builds a template path under the resolved checkout root at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:34-45`, and `validateDesignAction()` immediately reads it at line 68. For submodule guide installs, `GuideDetector.detectLocal()` checks the guide directory at `packages/core/src/guides/GuideDetector.ts:57-62`, and `GuideManager.ensureCheckout()` exists specifically to initialize uninitialized submodule checkouts before read commands (`packages/core/src/guides/GuideManager.ts:186-217`). Other commands that consume guide content call `ensureGuideReady()` (`packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts:81-82`, `packages/cli/src/commands/prompt.ts:63`, `packages/cli/src/commands/setup-ide.ts:105`; helper at `packages/cli/src/utils/guideReady.ts:17-31`), but this new command does not. A fresh clone with an uninitialized guide submodule can therefore reach `loadRequiredHeadings()` (`packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:52-61`) with no template and receive a `cf guides update` message instead of using the repository’s standard auto-init path. Call `ensureGuideReady(project.projectPath, checkoutRoot)` before resolving/reading the template and add coverage for that guide state.

findings.title: Indented fenced code blocks can be treated as real headings
findings.description: `documentHeadingKeys()` only toggles fenced-code state when `line.startsWith('```')` at `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignValidator.ts:63`. Markdown fenced blocks may be indented by up to three spaces, so a valid indented fence such as `  ```markdown` is not recognized; example headings inside the block are then counted as document headings and can satisfy required headings in `missingHeadings()` at line 81, producing false PASS results. This conflicts with the project’s parsing rule to prefer lenient parsing over strict formatting matching. The current fence test only covers column-zero fences (`packages/core/tests/schema/sliceDesignValidator.test.ts:84-87`). Use a fence detector such as `/^\s{0,3}```/` and add a test for indented fences.

findings.title: `--json` error-path tests bypass structured error mode
findings.description: The `--json` error cases at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate-design.test.ts:205-212` only assert empty stdout, no console output, and exit code 2. `run()` at lines 127-131 creates a bare Commander program and registers the command directly, so the real CLI bootstrap that detects `--json` and calls `setJsonMode()` (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:178-180`) never runs. As a result, `handleError()` takes its human-output branch in these tests (`packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:50-65`), and the structured `{ error: true, ... }` stderr contract is not exercised for no-arguments, missing-file, or missing-template errors. Enable JSON error mode in these tests via `setJsonMode()`/`CF_JSON=1` and parse stderr as JSON so the machine-readable failure contract is actually pinned.
